fields.expected: The work I'm proudest of is ClarityAtlas, an iOS health product I built end to end as technical lead and co-founder of Open Health Intelligence. The hard technical problem was estimating sleep without a wearable, so I built a passive sleep-estimation system from phone-interaction and motion signals using HealthKit and Core Motion inputs like step count, gait speed, and movement patterns, with Swift, SwiftUI, and Supabase behind it. I also built backend services for behavioral comparison, including a "Sleep Twins" matching system based on standardized features and weighted distance. We shipped it into a live pilot at Johns Hopkins with 30+ users, got into the Pava Spark Accelerator and NSF I-Corps, and presented to Hopkins President Ron Daniels and leadership from the Data Science and AI Institute. What I took from it was that the build is only part of making something real; recruiting users, talking to stakeholders, and repeatedly explaining why the thing should exist mattered just as much.
